newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali Prime Minister leaves on a visit to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Nepali Prime Minister leaves on a visit to Britain.

text.p: Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba of Nepal left on Sunday for a three-day visit to Britain to seek more investment for his country's aid-dependent economy, a Foreign Ministry official said.
"It is a good-will visit. We will discuss bilateral matters," Deuba told reporters before departing. He gave no details.
Deuba was scheduled to meet Prime Minister John Major, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, officials said.

It was the first official visit to London by a prime minister of the tiny Himalayan kingdom in 88 years. Chandra Shumshere Jung Bahadur Rana was the last Nepali prime minister to visit Britain in 1908.
Britain is a major aid donor to Nepal, one of the world's 10 poorest countries. About 60 percent of its economic development comes from Western donors, including the World Bank.
Deuba will address the Confederation of British Industries and speak at the London School of Economics. After London, he travels to Rome for the World Food Summit and returns to Nepal on November 18.
